title: Multi-Patch Clamp Recording
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bep2jdqe
materials: Mouse brain slices in ACSF.IV (SOP AF0099)
Pasteur Pipette (BD Falcon 357575), tip cut off
PTFE 0.22 µl syringe filter (Tisch Scientific SF17504)
Alexa Fluor 488 Hydrazide (Thermo Fisher Scientific A10436)
Cascade Blue Hydrazide, Trisodium salt (Thermo Fisher Scientific C687)
PF0285 DAB Detection of Biocytin Labeled Tissue
PF0289 Post Patch Clamp Slice Fixation
PF0299 Pulling Pipettes using the DMZ-Zeitz Universal
RP0234 Electrode Internal Solution with Biocytin II

steps.title: Initial System Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the recording chamber and hardware for the session.

substeps.instruction: Start running MilliQ water or ACSF through tubing to the chamber at least 30 minutes prior to recording.
Place the harp in the chamber and dip the 40x objective into the running solution to clean it.
Turn on the cooler and set it to 4°C.
Pull glass pipettes according to SOP PF0299, ensuring a tip resistance between 3-6 MΩ.

steps.title: Prepare Internal Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare the pipette filling solution and dye.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve an aliquot of internal solution (SOP RP0234) and appropriate dye from the freezer; place in the 4°C cooler until it reaches temperature.
For single transgenic specimens, use Alexa Fluor 488 dye.
Once thawed, mix 5 µl of dye into the internal solution and vortex to incorporate.
Load the mixed solution into a 1 ml syringe.
Obtain tissue slices using SOP AF0099 (Mouse) or SOP PF0295 (Human).
Incubate mouse tissue in ACSF.IV solution for at least 1 hour, but no more than 5 hours.
Incubate human tissue in ACSF.IV solution for at least 1 hour (can be indefinitely).

steps.title: Software and Hardware Setup
steps.instruction: Initialize the recording software and headstages.

substeps.instruction: Perform regular maintenance following the MultiPatch Maintenance document (Appendix 10.6).
Open IgorPro-64bit and run MultiPatch Configuration.
Open ACQ4 Manager and load Data Manager, Camera, and Multipatch modules.
Record relevant experiment meta-data from the Laboratory Information Management System.
Turn on the required headstages using the Control Pad.

steps.title: Load Slice into Chamber
steps.instruction: Position the brain slice for recording.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the heater and allow the bath to reach temperature.
Load the slice on the stage using a Pasteur pipette.
Gently position the tissue in the center of the recording chamber using a paintbrush.
Use forceps to set the harp across the slice.
Acquire a mosaic image of the entire slice under 4x and position the field of view over the area of interest.

steps.title: Prepare Pipettes
steps.instruction: Fill and mount the recording pipettes.

substeps.instruction: Fill eight pipettes with internal solution up to or just past the shoulder.
Load pipettes into headstages by sliding the glass pipette onto the silver wire and tightening the holding screw.
Secure the cross-talk shield in place alongside each pipette.
Find a region within the ROI with patchable cells.
Set the surface of the slice.
Identify healthy cells at least >= 40 µm below the surface.
Use the control pad to select up to 8 cells in a reasonable spatial arrangement.

steps.title: Patch Cells
steps.instruction: Establish seals with the target cells.

substeps.instruction: Select the pipette for the current target.
Use Approach mode to apply positive pressure and bring the pipette into the bath above the slice.
Verify positive pressure and ensure the tip is intact with a resistance of 3-6 MΩ; if not, retract and move to the next cell.
Send the pipette on an approach path to the cell target.
Switch to the native headstage control pad and use the X-axis turn dial in Approach mode to advance the pipette into the slice, avoiding other cells or vessels.
Reconfirm the target cell via fluorescent expression and adjust as necessary.
When the tip is on the cell and a dimple forms, enter Seal mode.
Apply negative pressure (either via user control or auto-seal) until a 1 GΩ giga-seal is produced.

If a giga-seal is obtained, lock the pipette using the Multipatch Control Pad. If a loose seal (< 1 GΩ) or spontaneous break-in occurs, the cell may be kept for observation. If not viable, de-select the headstage.
Repeat for all remaining pipettes.

steps.title: Perform Recordings
steps.instruction: Break into cells and acquire electrophysiological data.

substeps.instruction: If at least 2 pipettes have successful giga-seals, proceed; otherwise, choose new targets or a new slice.
Return to pipettes with giga-seals and break into the cell using Auto Break In or User mode.
Verify successful break-in by checking for low DC offset and low access resistance.
If at least 2 cells are recorded, continue with the Recording and Stimulation Protocol.
Concurrently obtain image stacks under IR, fluorescent cell reporter channels, and fluorescent pipette fill channel.

steps.title: Experiment Termination and Cleanup
steps.instruction: End the recording and clean the system.

substeps.instruction: Slowly pull off the cells to end the experiment.
Use the Multipatch Control Pad to turn back on any headstages that were turned off during patching.
Retract all pipettes and reseal if possible.
Once pipettes are well above the slice surface, turn off holding currents and apply positive pressure until the seal blows out.
Measure pipette drift.
Transfer the slice to a histology well plate with 4% PFA/2% glutaraldehyde following SOP PF0289.
Label the well plate using the format multi_YYYYMMDD _21_A01 (where 21 is the plate number and A01 is the row/column).
Discard used pipettes in a sharps container.
Turn off the heater and light sources.
Place the bubbler and solution line into a bottle of MilliQ water and flush the chamber for at least 10 minutes.
Discard ACSF.IX down the drain and rinse the bottle with MilliQ water.
Remove the bubbler and solution line from the water bottle, turn off the pump, and open it.
Dispense 70% EtOH into the chamber and allow it to run through the line.
Turn off the Carbogen airflow.
